status_summary: No term limit for NIH institute directors or other top career leaders was found to be in effect since 2025-01-20. Two bills introduced in February 2025, the NIH Reform Act (S. 664 and H.R. 1497), would replace NIAID with three institutes whose directors would be Senate-confirmed and serve five-year terms with one reappointment; both remain in committee, cover only those three posts rather than top career leaders across NIH, and contain no block grant, so they are a partial match. A March 2026 report cited an anonymous senior HHS official saying term limits were under discussion, and stated that institute directors still serve renewable five-year terms. No bill or proposal to block-grant NIH's grants budget to states was found. A January 2021 HHS final rule on five-year terms for some component directors predates the period.

timeline.event: The NIH Reform Act (S. 664) was introduced and referred to the Senate HELP Committee, with a House companion (H.R. 1497) introduced and referred to Energy and Commerce on 2025-02-21. The text replaces NIAID with three institutes whose Senate-confirmed directors would serve five-year terms with one reappointment; it sets no NIH-wide term limits and no block grants. No later action is recorded.

title: Term limits for top NIH career leaders; Congress to consider NIH block grants to states
uncertainties: The two Undark articles were read; the claim that term limits are under discussion rests on one anonymous official in one article. Federal Register searches (NIH only and all agencies) found no rule or notice on NIH term limits or block grants since 2025-01-20, and none for a rotational program rule from 2021 onward; the Unified Agenda listing was unreachable and the NIH proposed-rule listing was empty. The January 2021 HHS rule did not cover NIH institute directors, who already serve renewable five-year terms under earlier law per the sources. One congress.gov and GovInfo search found the NIH Reform Act (S. 664 and H.R. 1497); the Senate text and both bill status records were read on GovInfo on 2026-10-18 and show referral in February 2025 with no later action. The House text was checked only through its status record and title. The NIH newsroom and news searches showed no announced term limit policy. NIH policy pages and FY2026 or FY2027 budget documents were not searched for block grant language, so a budget proposal could have been missed. The stage rests on a judgment that the bill's two-term cap is a partial match: it applies to three posts that the bill would also make Senate-confirmed, so they would not be career positions as the recommendation describes; not_started 0 is the alternative if the term clause is read as incidental to the reorganization of NIAID.
